His elongated head made him stand out among his peers on the Jedi High Council, but also gave him a stately, introspective appearance.<ref name="TPMnovel">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref><ref name="AOTCnovel" /> Mundi had great empathy for other living beings, particularly his fellow Jedi. During his meditations in the Clone Wars, he preferred to have drops of water falling on his head because each drop reminded him of a Jedi who fell in battle. As a Jedi Master, Mundi had no fear of death, and believed that to die simply meant becoming one with the [[Living Force/Legends|Living Force]]. Mundi believed the greatest honor was to sacrifice oneself for others and for a greater cause.<ref name="Vanish" /> During his time as a Jedi General during the Clone Wars, Mundi believed that as a leader, he should not only give orders his forces but personally lead them into battle. During battle against the Droid Army on Aargonar, fellow Jedi Bultar Swan questioned his decision to monitor the battlefield from a LAAT/i gunships because it placed him in mortal jeopardy by exposing his position, but Mundi insisted it was his duty as a leader. Mundi demonstrated a strong ability to rally his troops and encourage their trust in the Force in the face of overwhelming odds, such as during the battles at Aargonar and Hypori.<ref name="Republic59" /><ref name="CW20" />

When he was granted the rare exception of being allowed to marry, as a husband and father Mundi had to face a difficult struggle to find the balance between attachment and love, but managed to do so.<ref name="Republic62" /> Although he cared for his family and loved them, Mundi was able to remain a Jedi Knight above everything else. This was particularly evident when, after his family was killed following the Battle of Cerea, Mundi was able overcome his grief during a situation in which other Jedi would risk falling to the dark side of the Force.<ref name="FF140" />

His shrewdness was illustrated when, near the end of the Clone Wars, Mundi recognized not only Palpatine's increasing efforts to expand his own power, but the political ramifications that the Jedi Order could face if they attempted to challenge Palpatine's power directly.<ref name="ROTSnovel" />

Mundi harbored a deep love of his homeworld of Cerea, and felt the Cereans were in perfect harmony with nature. Like many other Cereans of his generation, Mundi was suspicious and distrustful of technology and preferred that his home planet remain technologically primitive and relatively isolated from the rest of the galaxy. Although drawn to off-worlder technology during his youth, Mundi in his adulthood came to respect what his Cerean ancestors had built, such as the planetary capital, Tecave City. He also came to look upon the Outsider Citadels, more modern cities built by off-worlders, with disgust and contempt. Mundi spoke so passionately about this subject that, when arguing against Silais' offer to join the Republic, he immediately persuaded the Council of Elders to reject the proposal after a single speech.<ref name="Prelude1" /> Mundi did not completely oppose the use of all technology, but felt that it should be used in moderation and not simply for the sake of having it.<ref name="Prelude2" /> Although he was able to find beauty in other worlds,<ref name="Malastare2" /> Mundi felt uncomfortable on technologically-advanced planets when he left Cerea for Jedi business&mdash;particularly on the cities of the capital planet Coruscant&mdash;and feared Cerea would one day become like them.<ref name="Outlander2" />

Despite his wisdom and mindfulness, Mundi was not infallible. He could occasionally fall victim to his own pride, as when, after successfully arguing against Silais's offer to join the Republic, Mundi believed himself invincible and tried to sway the minds of a youthful Pro-Tech rally, inadvertently making them angrier.<ref name="Prelude1" /> Mundi demonstrated more of these prideful features during his younger years. When encouraged by Yoda during a training session to watch his blind spot in combat, the adolescent Mundi boasted that he did not have a blind spot.<ref name="Prelude3" /> Similarly, when he first confronted the raiders on his homeworld, Mundi believed he was too strong for the enemy to possibly defeat him, which nearly cost him the battle. He also showed fallibility by secretly wishing for a son instead of a daughter, but eventually he realized how foolish this desire was.<ref name="Prelude5" />

When Qui-Gon Jinn theorized that the Sith had reemerged following his duel with Darth Maul, Mundi claimed that the return of the Sith was "impossible" because (as far as the Jedi knew) they had been extinct.<ref name="TPM" /> Likewise, given Mundi's past experience with Count Dooku he refused to believe that the former respectable Jedi master become a murderous schemer.<ref name="AOTCfilm" /><ref name="FF140" />

When Padawan Ahsoka Tano framed for treason, Mundi, alongside the rest of the Jedi Council, stripped her of her status as a Jedi and turned her over to the Republic military court, in order to not oppose to the Senate's will. Due to the many circumstantial evidence against Tano, he believed her to be guilty. After Tano was proven innocent and the real traitor apprehended, Mundi joined the Council in offering to reinstate Tano into the Jedi Order, apologized and praised her efforts to prove her innocence, even stating that she had shown the true signs of a Jedi Knight.<ref name="TWJ">{{TCW|The Wrong Jedi}}</ref> When Master Yoda heard the voice of the late Qui-Gon Jinn, Mundi feared that he had become deceived by the Sith.<ref name="Voices">{{TCW|Voices}}</ref>

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|Of all living Jedi, have you only the skills to defeat Sharad Hett.''"<br />"''You flatter me, Master Yoda.''"<br />"''The truth only, I speak.|Yoda and Ki-Adi-Mundi|<ref name="Outlander1" />}}
[[File:Lightsaber_mundi.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Ki-Adi-Mundi's [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] (blue blade)]]
By the time of the Clone Wars, Ki-Adi-Mundi was considered by many to be one of the best swordsmen in the Jedi Order.<ref name="TCWA:LD">[[Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures (video game)|''Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures'']]</ref> Mundi was a powerful practitioner of [[Form IV/Legends|Form IV, Ataru]], and was second only to Grandmaster Yoda in his mastery of the style, and was rivaled only by Agen Kolar.<ref name="CW2DVD">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Two|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season Two]]</ref> Mundi also mastered [[Form III/Legends|Form III, Soresu]], and was highly proficient with it. He was also very skilled in [[Form II/Legends|Form II, Makashi]].<ref name=":0" /> His lightsaber prowess was particularly demonstrated during his duel with General Grievous on Hypori, where he not only survived the fight, but was the only one out of six Jedi to still be standing by the end of the duel. Despite getting disarmed and nearly killed, Mundi was able to successfully defend himself against a combat style which had never been seen before by the Jedi, as Hypori marked Grievous' first appearance against a Jedi who lived to recall the experience, as well as being fatigued and having his Force Augmentation greatly weakened by the deaths of the Jedi around him.<ref name="CW21" /> Likewise, Mundi engaged the Dark Jedi Asajj Ventress on Coruscant and not only survived the duel, but fought Ventress to a stalemate and forced her to retreat.<ref name="TCW2" /> He also often performed a [[Shiim/Legends|glancing cut]] with his lightsaber in combat.<ref name="H2H" /> Mundi had extremely fast reflexes which allowed him to react in time to briefly defend himself after his clone troopers attacked him following the issuance of Order 66. While he was ultimately killed in the encounter, Mundi was able to deflect several shots and kill three of his attackers before they killed him.<ref name="ROTS" /><ref name="Order66" />

[[File:KiAdiMundi-SWJPE.png|thumb|right|200px|Mundi was a master of Form IV and also proficient in Form II.]]
Mundi was also skilled in the use of several Force powers. As a child he could [[Telekinesis/Legends|float items with his mind]], though without training he sometimes made them [[Combustion|detonate]].<ref name="Prelude4" /> Early in life he undid his bonds and turned aside a thrown dagger with his powers.<ref name="Prelude6" /> During his duel with Grievous, Mundi displayed the ability to produce powerful telekinetic blasts capable of creating a crater in the ground.<ref name="CW21" /> The Cerean could also [[Force jump/Legends|leap incredible heights]], such as when he launched himself onto a moving gunship during his battle with Ventress.<ref name="TCW2" /> He was also able to use [[Force healing/Legends|Force healing]] to some degree, as proven when he healed a broken collar bone after the skiff he was riding on crashed during his mission to find Sharad Hett on Tatooine.<ref name="Outlander3" /> His mental powers included being able to [[Force empathy/Legends|sense Anakin Skywalker's feelings]].<ref name="TPM" />

Beyond his abilities with the Force, Mundi was a competent pilot. Mundi survived starfighter dogfighting against pirates in the Voronat system,<ref name="Republic62" /> and directly engaged Aurra Sing in space combat in Talas.<ref name="HuntSing1" /> Additionally, while rescuing his daughter Sylvn from Jabba Desilijic Tiure on Tatooine, Mundi successfully performed a tricky maneuver in which he brought his ship nearly to the planet's surface, creating a sandstorm that clogged the air intakes of his enemies' atmospheric flyers, thus destroying them.<ref name="Prelude6" /> Mundi could also speak fluent [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]] in addition to [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]].<ref name="Outlander2" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Concept and design===
{{Quote|When I first saw the design, I just thought it was amazing, because it incorporates so many different things. To me, he looks part Native American and part European, and he's got a wonderful, wise face. Once I'd seen that design, I had a pretty good idea of what he should be like.|[[Silas Carson]]|<ref name="SWI55">[[Star Wars Insider 55|''Star Wars Insider'' 55]]</ref>}}
[[File:MundiConceptArt.jpg|thumb|right|140px|Concept art of Ki-Adi-Mundi for ''The Phantom Menace''.]]
[[File:Ki_adi_mundi_eyepatch_concept_art.jpg|thumb|left|120px|Ultimately unused concept art of Ki-Adi-Mundi from ''Revenge of the Sith'']]
Ki-Adi-Mundi was designed by artistic director and concept designer [[Iain McCaig]] for the first film of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[prequel trilogy]], [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']] ([[1999]]). The design for what eventually became Mundi began when ''Star Wars'' creator and executive producer [[George Lucas]] asked McCaig to draw sketches for alien characters to be featured on the Jedi High Council. In doing so, McCaig experimented by drawing some unusual parodies of the elderly Obi-Wan Kenobi, including one with whale-like features, with an elongated head and ridges along the back of the neck.<ref name="The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace]]''</ref> While drawing early conceptual sketches of the Jedi characters for the final film in the trilogy, [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']] ([[2005]]), concept artist [[Derek Thompson]] proposed a version of Mundi that had lost his left eye during the battles of the Clone Wars and now wore an [[Eye patch/Legends|eye patch]] along with a black and gold cape. The concept was ultimately not used in the final film.<ref name="The Art of Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith">''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode III: Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref>

Although originally designed for ''The Phantom Menace'', Mundi was featured as the protagonist in the [[Star Wars: Prelude to Rebellion|''Prelude to Rebellion'']] story arc of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series ''[[Star Wars: Republic|Star Wars]]'' ([[1998]]), the [[Star Wars (1998) 1|first issue]] of which was released in [[December]] 1998. This makes that comic book series Mundi's first formal appearance in the ''Star Wars'' universe, not ''The Phantom Menace'', which was released in [[May]] 1999.<ref name="SWI44" /><ref>Szadkowski, Joseph (April 10, 1999). "The future Darth Vader confronts his fear, dreams". [[Wikipedia:The Washington Times|''The Washington Times'']]: p. B4</ref> Due to his large, oval-shaped head, Mundi has often been compared to the [[Wikipedia:Coneheads|Coneheads]], the big-headed alien characters played by [[Wikipedia:Dan Aykroyd|Dan Aykroyd]], [[Wikipedia:Jane Curtin|Jane Curtin]] and [[Wikipedia:Laraine Newman|Laraine Newman]].<ref>Vancheri, Barbara (May 20, 1999). "Fanning the Force; At local theaters, 'Phantom Menace' brings out a crowd, camaraderie and compliments". [[Wikipedia:Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|''Pittsburgh Post-Gazette'']]: p. C1</ref> This reference was even featured in a ''Star Wars'' medium, when the clone instructor Kal Skirata disparagingly referred to him as a Conehead.<ref name="TrueColors" />

===Film portrayal===
{{Quote|I enjoy playing this very wise man who is part of the great council. You get the feeling that he is kind of like your uncle, because he's this nice, kind, wise, protective master. I always think that way of him.|[[Silas Carson]]|<ref name="SWI55" />}}
Ki-Adi-Mundi was portrayed by [[Silas Carson]] in all three prequel films. Carson also portrayed the characters Nute Gunray, [[Lott Dod/Legends|Lott Dod]] and [[Antidar Williams/Legends|Antidar Williams]] in those films. Carson originally auditioned for the supporting role of a fighter pilot role, but the character was eliminated from the script a few days after the audition.<ref name="SWI55" /> However, George Lucas screened a video of Silas' audition and was so impressed he encouraged the actor to accept the role of Mundi,<ref name="EHerald">{{BookCite|container=Actor Silas tackles three roles in Phantom|title=Evening Herald|date=1999-07-14}}</ref> which led him to play the other parts as well. In addition to appearing on-screen, Carson also performed Mundi's voice, mimicking that of an elderly man who speaks slowly and deliberately. During the filming of ''The Phantom Menace'', executive producer George Lucas had not yet decided whether he would keep Carson's voice or dub in that of another actor, as he had done for several other characters, but Lucas found he liked Carson's vocal performance and decided to keep it.<ref name="SWI55" /><ref>Hendry, Steve (July 15, 1999). "The light fantastic". [[Wikipedia:Edinburgh Evening News|''Edinburgh Evening News'']].</ref> To create Mundi's movements, Carson spent time with elderly people and watched the ways they moved and spoke. In crafting Mundi's manner of speech, Carson said he spoke slowly not only because of the Jedi's age, but because he believed Mundi was wise and would not waste his words.<ref name="SWI44" />

[[File:Lieutenant_Williams.png|thumb|right|180px|Ki-Adi-Mundi was portrayed in the prequel trilogy by Silas Carson, who also played Nute Gunray, Lott Dod and Antidar Williams.]]
Since Carson played many characters in ''The Phantom Menace'', he was one of the few actors who received the entire script during filming, rather than simply portions like most of the rest of the cast. During the filming of ''The Phantom Menace'', there were instances when Carson would play both Mundi and Gunray in different scenes on the same day. Lucas did not give Carson any backstory from which to build his performance as Mundi, but simply left it up to the actor to create. Once the shooting of each film was completed, Carson did not know right away whether he would be returning for the next film. According to ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' writer [[Scott Chernoff]], Lucas, producer [[Rick McCallum]] and casting director [[Robin Gurland]] were so impressed with Carsons' four performances in ''The Phantom Menace'' that they decided to expand upon Mundi's role in the second film.<ref name="SWI55" />

The Mundi costume and prosthetics were designed by the [[Industrial Light & Magic]] visual effects creature shop. They included a prosthetic head, fake hair and two cheek pieces that were built and glued onto Carson's face so they would actually move along with his facial reactions.<ref name="SWI44" /><ref name="Multiple Personality">{{InsiderCite|83|Multiple Personality}}</ref> During the first film, it took about four hours to apply Mundi's make-up and prosthetics,<ref name="SWI44" /> but in the later films the process was narrowed down to three hours. However, while the process took longer to prepare for Mundi than it did for Nute Gunray or Lott Dod, Carson said the Mundi make-up was less hot and comfortable to wear than those other character and that he would often walk around off-set and forget he had the make-up on at all.<ref name="SWI55" /><ref name="SWI44" /> During filming for [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']] ([[2002]]), the make-up artists used a different brand of make-up glues and removers, causing Silas' skin to break out due to allergies. Silas was trained by stunt coordinator [[Nick Gillard]] for his lightsaber scenes in ''Attack of the Clones''. Upon learning Mundi would be fighting in that film, Carson worked out a great deal before filming began to get physically fit, and claimed he was even outrunning some of the [[Wikipedia:Stunt performer|stunt performers]]. For these scenes, Carson decided that although Mundi appeared slow and frail at normal times, he should be fast and strong while fighting, although the actor struggled to maintain the balance between those two different aspects of the character.<ref name="SWI55" />

[[File:Ki-adi-mundi_green_lightsaber.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Ki-Adi-Mundi is shown with a green-bladed lightsaber, while he has a blue lightsaber in all other scenes.]]
Mundi is the only sitting Jedi High Council member other than Yoda and Windu to have a speaking role in the final cut of the first three films.<ref name="ROTS" /><ref name="TPM" /> In ''Attack of the Clones'', Mundi can be seen fighting with a green-bladed lightsaber during a shot when he stands back-to-back with Padmé Amidala. The character uses a blue-bladed lightsaber in every other shot in the film, including those that come immediately before and after that particular shot.<ref name="AOTCfilm" /> A scene was partially filmed for ''Attack of the Clones'' in which Mundi and Plo Koon led a group of Jedi on a raid of a Trade Federation ship during the battle of Geonosis. This scene did not appear in the final version of the film, but the rough cut and animatics later became available on the official website for registered [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] customers.<ref name="Hyperspace-Jedi Assault on the Droid Control Ship">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/video/droidcontrolship.html|text=Jedi Assault on the Droid Control Ship}}</ref> That rough cut was also included among the deleted scenes for ''Attack of the Clones'' in the ''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'' [[Wikipedia:Blu-ray Disc|Blu-ray]] collection, which was released in September [[2011]].<ref name="BlurayScene" />

===Other appearances and merchandise===
{{Quote|In fairness to the publishing team at the time, they got this all vetted through the channels they were supposed to and thought they were good, but had no idea how much wet clay they were dealing with in making him a married knight on the council.|[[Pablo Hidalgo]], on Ki-Adi-Mundi's initial EU portrayal|<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|pabl0hidalgo|url=status/1805039958270558316|name=[[Pablo Hidalgo]]|quote=In fairness to the publishing team at the time, they got this all vetted through the channels they were supposed to and thought they were good, but had no idea how much wet clay they were dealing with in making him a married knight on the council.|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/5P7IF}}</ref>}}
''Prelude to Rebellion'' depicted Ki-Adi-Mundi as sitting on the Jedi Council as a married man who held the rank of Jedi Knight, which presented issues with later established canon.<ref name="Twitter" /> Ki-Adi-Mundi was voiced by [[Jess Harnell]] in the video games [[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']],<ref name="SW:OW" /> [[Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Jedi Power Battles'']],<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles">[[Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Jedi Power Battles'']]</ref> and ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]'',<ref name="Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]''</ref> and [[Corey Burton]] in ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''. The character was voiced by [[Daran Norris]] in the [[2003]] ''[[Star Wars: Clone Wars]]'' animated television series,<ref name="LegacyTerror" /> and [[Brian George]] in the [[2008]] [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|series]].<ref name="LaPR" /> Mundi also appeared, but was not voiced, in ''[[Star Wars: Battle for the Republic]]'', a [[THQ]] Wireless turn-based strategy video game where the characters appear as hero and villain squares that can be used for attack and defense. Mundi is one of the hero squares.<ref name="Star Wars: Battle for the Republic">''[[Star Wars: Battle for the Republic]]''</ref> Mundi could be unlocked as a playable character in the ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Video Game]]'' video game series (which his name is misspelled "Ki-Adi Mundi" from 2005 to 2007) by entering a cheat code or purchasing the character with tokens.<ref name="LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga">''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]''</ref> Additionally, players could purchase a costume pack for the video game ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'' (2008) allowing the player to change the main character Starkiller's appearance into that of Mundi.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://blogcritics.org/gaming/article/playstation-network-update-11132008/page-2|text=PlayStation Network Update: 11/13/2008 - Page 2|author=Prince, Michael|date=2008-11-14|nobackup=1}}</ref>

[[File:Ki-adi-mundi_action_figure.jpg|thumb|right|120px|The Ki-Adi-Mundi action figure from Hasbro's ''Star Wars: Episode I'' toy line]]
[[File:Ki-adi-mundi_lego_minifigure.jpg|thumb|left|150px|The Ki-Adi-Mundi LEGO minifigure]]
The first Ki-Adi-Mundi action figure was produced in 1999 as part of [[Hasbro]]'s [[Star Wars: Episode I (toy line)|''Star Wars: Episode I'' toy line]] of three and 3/4 inch figures.<ref>Chetwynd, Josh; Soriano, Csar G. (May 3, 1999). "Reaching for the 'Star Wars' tie-ins, from linens to pools". [[Wikipedia:USA Today|''USA Today'']]</ref><ref>Courter, Barry (May 14, 1999). "May the Force protect your change purse". [[Wikipedia:Chattanooga Times Free Press|''Chattanooga Times Free Press'']]: p. E1.</ref> A 12-inch action figure of Mundi was also created in 1999 by [[Sideshow Collectibles]].<ref>Szadkowski, Joseph (September 3, 1999). "X-Men, Star Wars in action". [[Wikipedia:The Washington Times|''The Washington Times'']]: p. C10.</ref><ref>Szadkowski, Joseph (November 20, 2008). "Canary, Kenobi on shelves". [[Wikipedia:The Washington Times|''The Washington Times'']]: p. C09.</ref> In 2006, a holographic action figure of Mundi was released as part of Hasbro's ''[[Star Wars: The Saga Collection]]'' toy line.<ref name="Star Wars: The Saga Collection">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: The Saga Collection|pack=#027: Holographic Ki-Adi-Mundi|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/tsc027kiadimundi.asp}}</ref> The visual concept of Mundi wearing an eye patch designed by Derek Thompson was used as the basis of a 2009 action figure from Hasbro's ''[[Star Wars: The Legacy Collection]]'' line.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://jedi-business.com/figureDetails.aspx?ID=333|text=Ki-Adi Mundi Action Figure|archivedate=20101126170951}}</ref> [[Wikipedia:Don Post|Don Post Studios]] also developed a latex Ki-Adi-Mundi mask.<ref>O'Brien, Pat (May 20, 2005). "'Star Wars': Merchandising reawakens; Memento Force is strong". [[Wikipedia:The Press-Enterprise (California)|''The Press-Enterprise'']]: p. D01.</ref> A [[Wikipedia:Lego minifigure|Lego minifigure]] of Mundi, with a removable head-piece, was created for the [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO ''Star Wars'']] [[Nantex-class territorial defense starfighter/Legends|Geonosian starfighter]] box set in 2011.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.fbtb.net/2011/07/28/7959-geonosian-starfighter-review|text=Review: 7959 Geonosian Starfighter|author=Martin, Nick|date=2011-07-28|archivedate=20170707220551}}</ref>

Mundi made a non-canonical appearance in a flashback in [[Star Wars (1998) 41|''Star Wars'' (1998) 41]], the 41st issue of ''[[Star Wars: Republic]]'' comic book series by Dark Horse Comics. The story features the Devaronian [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Vilmarh Grahrk]] describing his own, obviously false and exaggerated version of his encounters with the Jedi Council. Grahrk describes returning a lost treasure to the Jedi Council, prompting each of its members, including Mundi, to drop to their hands and knees and literally worship him out of gratitude.<ref name="Star Wars 1998 41">[[Star Wars (1998) 41|''Star Wars'' (1998) 41]]</ref>

===Retcons===
{{Quote|I have heard of a Cerean Jedi Master named Ki-Adi-Mundi. Is he not married?"<br />"Because of the low birthrate of Cereans, Master Ki-Adi-Mundi is exempt from the Jedi edict that discourages marriage."<br />"And has he been married long?"<br />"He has been with his wives for many years."<br />"Wives? How many does he have?"<br />"Two. As I said, the Cerean birthrate is very low.|The [[Margravine]] [[Quenelle]] ([[Skull Queen]]) inquires of Jedi Knights [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Bultar Swan/Legends|Bultar Swan]] about Mundi's marriage|<ref name="SWA3">''[[Star Wars Adventures 3: The Hostage Princess]]''</ref>}}
When Ki-Adi-Mundi was first introduced in ''Prelude to Rebellion'', he was engaged in a polygamous marriage and had children. This comic book series was released prior to the knowledge that the Jedi Order discourages marriage, as revealed in the film ''Attack of the Clones''. To explain the continuity error created by Mundi's family, a [[Retroactive continuity|retcon]] was later established that due to the Cerean gender ratio of 20 females to 1 male, Mundi was granted an exception to allow the continuation of his species.<ref name="SWA3" /><ref name="Republic62" />

In [[Star Wars (1998) 8|''Star Wars'' (1998) 8]], Mundi says that he's "not yet a Master"<ref name="SW8">[[Star Wars (1998) 8|''Star Wars'' (1998) 8]]</ref> and several ''Star Wars'' reference books such as ''[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace Scrapbook]]'' and ''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' mentioned that Mundi was the sole Jedi Knight on the Jedi High Council, while the others were Masters.<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace Scrapbook">''[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace Scrapbook]]''</ref><ref name="The New Essential Guide to Characters">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> This conflicted with dialogue in ''Revenge of the Sith'', when Anakin Skywalker becomes angry that he is appointed to the Council without being promoted to Jedi Master, and claims it has never happened in the history of the Jedi. Since the films remain the highest level of [[canon]] at G-canon, the Expanded Universe and the [[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]] established that Mundi's promotion to Jedi Master was still in progress right before the Naboo crisis.<ref name="Databank" />
